candidates.summary: Norwegian police and the PST security service said they were investigating telecommunications company Telenor on suspicion of aiding crimes against humanity in Myanmar and violating sanctions. Investigators raided Telenor’s Oslo headquarters on Tuesday. Telenor said it was cooperating and argued that employees in Myanmar had faced severe risks if they did not comply with military orders. No individuals had been charged or placed under investigation.
candidates.title: Norwegian police raid Telenor headquarters in Myanmar-related investigation

candidates.summary: United Nations officials said the Ebola epidemic in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo remained large and was still growing in some areas, although containment efforts were showing progress elsewhere. Government figures published Tuesday listed 7,258 confirmed cases and 3,510 deaths across seven provinces. WHO official Olivier le Polain said it was too early to conclude that the outbreak had passed its peak.
candidates.title: UN says eastern Congo Ebola outbreak remains extensive despite some progress

candidates.summary: U.S. presidential envoy John Coale met Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko for their first talks in six months. Washington has sought additional prisoner releases in exchange for sanctions relief. Belarusian state media said Coale conveyed President Donald Trump’s support for the negotiations. Human-rights group Viasna says Belarus still holds more than 900 political prisoners; Lukashenko rejects that characterization.
candidates.title: US envoy meets Lukashenko for renewed prisoner-release talks

candidates.summary: Ukraine’s Brigadier-General Andrii Biletskyi announced an offensive operation named Vivaldi in northern Donetsk region. He said Ukrainian forces had cleared Russian infiltration groups from 75 square kilometers, recaptured another 10 square kilometers and taken control of several villages or surrounding areas. Reuters said it could not independently verify the territorial claims.
candidates.title: Ukrainian commander announces offensive operation in northern Donetsk

candidates.summary: Rail services across central and northern Netherlands were disrupted during Tuesday’s morning rush after pipes were deliberately attached to tracks at about 20 locations, infrastructure operator ProRail said. Several road level crossings also remained closed. ProRail described the incidents as deliberate human-caused disruption but said the responsible party and motive were unknown; national police opened an investigation.
candidates.title: Deliberately placed pipes disrupt Dutch rail network

candidates.summary: Independent United Nations experts reported that Belarusian courts, police, security services, prosecutors and prison authorities had acted in a coordinated manner to repress government critics throughout the justice process. The panel cited arbitrary arrests, torture, denial of legal safeguards, closed trials and harassment after release. Belarus has previously rejected UN criticism and did not immediately respond to the new findings.
candidates.title: UN experts report systematic justice-system abuses in Belarus

priorStories.headline: Houthis capture two Red Sea islands
priorStories.body:
Yemen’s Houthi rebels took control of the Greater and Lesser Hanish islands after government-allied forces withdrew, according to two Yemeni government officials and a Houthi official.

The islands are in the southern Red Sea, about 160 kilometers north of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a major shipping route.

priorStories.headline: Israeli strikes in Lebanon kill 13
priorStories.body:
Israeli strikes on a town in southern Lebanon killed at least 13 people, including six children, according to Lebanon’s Health Ministry.

The attacks came during several days of escalating strikes despite a ceasefire reached by Israel and Hezbollah in June.

priorStories.headline: Saudi oil pipeline faces weeks of repairs
priorStories.body:
Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline is expected to remain mostly out of service for three to five weeks after an attack last week damaged the line and a major pumping facility, two regional officials briefed on repairs said.

One official said limited oil movements might continue while repairs are underway.

priorStories.headline: Supreme Court keeps mail-ballot rules unchanged
priorStories.body:
The Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s emergency request to permit new restrictions on mail ballots before November’s midterm elections.

The brief order said the administration was unlikely to prevail in court. Justices Samuel Alito and Clarence Thomas publicly dissented. Existing state mail-ballot processes remain in effect while the litigation continues.

candidates.summary: Police dispersed opposition demonstrations in Kinshasa, Lubumbashi and Uvira against proposed constitutional changes that critics say could permit President Felix Tshisekedi to seek a third term. Reuters witnesses reported tear gas and warning shots in Kinshasa after clashes between protesters and government supporters. Several hundred people participated in the capital; authorities had prohibited the protests in Lubumbashi and Uvira.
candidates.title: Congolese police disperse protests against proposed constitutional changes

candidates.summary: Britain announced that it would upgrade diplomatic relations with Venezuela by appointing an ambassador. The British government said the move was intended to support its role in a transition to democracy and did not endorse Venezuela’s disputed 2024 election or any political faction. Venezuela welcomed the decision.
candidates.title: Britain announces upgraded diplomatic relations with Venezuela

candidates.summary: A British public inquiry found that failures by senior staff and dysfunctional management at the Countess of Chester Hospital allowed nurse Lucy Letby to harm infants and that at least two murders could have been prevented through earlier action. The report recommended stronger neonatal safeguards, including protocols for suspected deliberate harm and consideration of cameras in cots and incubators. It did not examine Letby’s guilt or innocence.
candidates.title: Lucy Letby inquiry finds hospital failures left infants unprotected

candidates.summary: Italy and Spain extended temporary border controls between the two countries for another 15 days. Italy cited continuing internal-security risks and a potential threat of terrorist infiltration, while Spain said the conditions justifying the controls remained in place and that its measures would continue until October 8. The controls were introduced after a large migrant influx into Spain’s Ceuta enclave.
candidates.title: Italy and Spain extend temporary border controls

candidates.summary: The Kennedy Center board voted to close the Washington performing arts venue for up to two years for a $257 million renovation. The vote followed a federal judge’s order temporarily blocking the center from adding President Donald Trump’s name to its facade or renaming its campus for him without congressional approval. Trump subsequently said renovation would not begin while the naming dispute is under appeal.
candidates.title: Kennedy Center board votes to close venue for renovations

candidates.summary: The United States announced a visa-restriction policy targeting foreign nationals it considers responsible for South African laws or policies enabling uncompensated land seizures, racial discrimination or incitement of imminent violence against minority groups. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said South Africa had not adequately addressed previously stated U.S. concerns.
candidates.title: US announces South Africa-related visa restrictions

candidates.summary: The U.S. Senate voted 50-49 to advance the Clarity Act, falling 10 votes short of the 60 required. Four Republicans joined all Democrats in opposing the cryptocurrency-regulation bill. One Republican changed his vote for procedural reasons that preserve the option of reconsideration, but Congress’s approaching pre-election recess left the measure stalled.
candidates.title: US Senate blocks cryptocurrency regulation bill

candidates.summary: Argentina’s government submitted its proposed 2027 budget to Congress. The bill forecasts 4% economic growth, annual inflation of 18% and a trade surplus exceeding $15 billion in 2027. The proposal must proceed through the budget committee and Congress; the projections and spending plans have not been enacted.
candidates.title: Argentina submits proposed 2027 budget to Congress

candidates.summary: German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius and U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signed a letter of intent aimed at increasing cooperation between the two countries’ weapons industries. Pistorius said details of the cooperation and a planned German purchase of Tomahawk cruise missiles remained to be negotiated.
candidates.title: Germany and US sign defense-industry cooperation letter

candidates.summary: Colombian-born businessman and former Venezuelan minister Alex Saab pleaded guilty in Miami federal court to one count of conspiracy to launder money. Court records said Saab agreed to forfeit $195 million and cooperate with the U.S. Justice Department. Prosecutors accused him of diverting money from a Venezuelan food-assistance program and transferring some proceeds through U.S. accounts.
candidates.title: Alex Saab pleads guilty in US money-laundering case

candidates.summary: Republican U.S. Representative Thomas Massie filed privileged articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, alleging that Hegseth abused his office by carrying out hostilities against Iran without congressional approval. The privileged designation requires the House to consider the resolution within two legislative days. The Pentagon said the department remained united behind Hegseth.
candidates.title: Republican lawmaker files impeachment articles against Hegseth

candidates.summary: The Congressional Budget Office estimated that U.S. combat operations against Iran had cost the Defense Department about $38 billion through August 1 and could add about $3 billion a month, depending on the conflict’s intensity. It projected a 0.5% inflation increase in the first quarter of 2027 and said depleted munitions could take five years to replenish. The Pentagon disputed findings that its stocks were insufficient.
candidates.title: CBO estimates US combat operations against Iran have cost $38 billion

candidates.summary: New Zealand’s Parliament passed legislation implementing the country’s free-trade agreement with India by 93 votes to 29. The agreement would eliminate or significantly reduce Indian tariffs on about 95% of New Zealand exports, while Indian goods would receive duty-free access to New Zealand. The agreement will take effect only after both countries complete their ratification procedures.
candidates.title: New Zealand Parliament passes India trade-deal legislation

candidates.summary: A Saudi-led military coalition spokesperson said Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca before it entered prohibited airspace over the city. He described it as an attempt to target Mecca. A Houthi military source denied that the group posed a threat to Mecca or other Islamic holy sites.
candidates.title: Saudi coalition says air defenses intercepted Houthi drone near Mecca

candidates.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed at least five Palestinians, including two children and a Hamas commander, in northern and southern Gaza, according to health officials and Hamas sources. Medics said strikes on a vehicle in Sheikh Radwan killed two people and wounded seven, while a strike on a tent encampment in Mawasi killed two and wounded 14. Israel said it targeted a Hamas commander in the Rafah Brigade.
candidates.title: Israeli strikes kill at least five people in Gaza

candidates.summary: Indonesia’s Corruption Eradication Commission said it detained eight suspects, including Summarecon Agung’s president director and government officials, in an alleged land-rights bribery case. Investigators seized electronic evidence and cash in several currencies worth a combined 106.3 billion rupiah. The case concerns an application to extend building rights for land managed by the developer in Bogor, West Java. Summarecon did not immediately comment.
candidates.title: Indonesia detains eight suspects in land-rights bribery case

candidates.summary: Brazil’s Supreme Court postponed a decision on whether to open an investigation into Justice Alexandre de Moraes over allegations that he advised a banker accused of leading a multibillion-dollar fraud scheme. Justice Flavio Dino requested additional time to review the case, and proceedings stopped during procedural voting before the court began considering the merits. No investigation was authorized by the session.
candidates.title: Brazil Supreme Court postpones decision on proposed Moraes investigation

candidates.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine was testing a domestically developed weapon for intercepting drones and that it successfully destroyed an Iranian-designed Shahed drone overnight. He said technical aspects still required refinement. Ukraine’s military separately said it downed 187 airborne targets overnight; the reported performance and the new weapon’s capabilities were not independently verified.
candidates.title: Ukraine says new anti-drone weapon recorded successful test
